title: Man. Post. Cap. X: PLAC — then only reatus? Show ἁμαρτία used for bare guilt in Scripture
pass_a_gloss: Then bare guilt? If so, the enduring pre-law world-sin is only reatus. Give even one NT place—or at least an OT judgment-text—where ἁμαρτία means bare guilt alone. Why take so common a word here in a wholly unused sense? That first.
pass_b_english: Guilt? Therefore by the sin which lasted in the world until the law, bare guilt alone is to be understood.
Let there be given us, then, some place from the New Testament in which ἁμαρτία is used for bare guilt alone; or at least some place from the Old, where it is so used when God’s judgment is in view.
For why in this place should that word, so frequent, be taken in a sense altogether unused?
source_text: Reatus? Igitur per peccatum quod usque ad legem duravit in mundo, solus reatus intelligendus est. Detur igitur nobis locus aliquis e Novo Testamento in quo ἁμαρτία pro solo reatu usurpetur; aut detur saltem aliquis e Veteri, ubi sic usurpetur, cum de Dei iudicio agitur. Cur enim hoc loco vox illa, tam frequens, acciperetur sensu prorsus inusitato? Hoc primum.
